chunks: And with this chain of transmission, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Jamīl, from Zurārah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
"Rinsing the mouth and drawing water into the nose are not from wudu (ablution)." That is, they are not among the obligatory acts of wudu (ablution); this indicates that.

key_terms.الِاسْتِنْشَاقُ: Drawing water into the nose during purification
key_terms.الْمَضْمَضَةُ: Rinsing the mouth with water during purification
key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: The ritual ablution performed before acts such as salat (prayer)
key_terms.فَرَائِضِ: The obligatory duties or required acts

ai.seo_question: Are rinsing the mouth and nose obligatory in wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith states that rinsing the mouth and drawing water into the nose are not obligatory parts of wudu (ablution). It clarifies a legal distinction between the obligatory elements of wudu (ablution) and its recommended acts.
